# Methods decision ledger

One place for every decision that the Methods section of the MultiScholaR paper must be able to
state: what the software computes, what it offers, what it defaults to, what it refuses, how
results are recorded and reproduced, what was validated and how, what it requires, and what is out
of scope or deferred.

Built on 2026-11-18 from branch `performance-v2` at `591631d5`. Most of these decisions were until
now recorded only in ticket files under `tickets/`, which are not in the repository.

## How to use it

- The tables follow the paper's likely Methods subsections. One row is one decision.
- **Status** tells you whether a row may be written into the paper as a fact:
  - `in force`: the software does this on `performance-v2`. Where a row says "not verified in
    code", the source says so but nobody checked the code for this ledger.
  - `decided, not yet implemented`: decided, but the code is on a named branch or not written.
    The paper may state it only once it is merged.
  - `superseded by <id>`: kept for the history. Do not state it; state the row it points to.
  - `conflicts with <id>`: two sources disagree and nothing settles it. Settle it before writing.
  - `open`: a question nobody has answered yet. All of them are listed at the end.
  - `deferred`: explicitly left out, or left until after publication. Material for Limitations.
- **Decided by** is `user` only where a source records the author's decision. `default taken by
  best practice and recorded` means the implementer chose and wrote it down. Many answers of
  2026-11-11 rest on one blanket approval of a list of recommendations, and the calls of
  2026-11-15 were made under delegation; the cells say so. Read those rows before relying on them.
- **Basis** holds only what a source gives. `basis not recorded` means exactly that; nothing was
  inferred. Appendix B lists those rows. Citations appear only where a source carries them, with
  any caution the source attached (several quotes are still to be checked against the typeset
  papers). No citation was added from memory.
- **Evidence** is a repository path where the source is committed. "ticket KIT-nnn, not in the
  repository" means the only source is a git-ignored ticket: the ledger row is then the durable
  record.
- **State in the Methods as** is a starting phrase, not final text.
- Figures (memory, time, error rates) are quoted as their source wrote them. Check each against
  the file named in its Evidence cell before it goes into the paper.
- All validation so far is on synthetic data. Real-data runs are deferred to the end.
- Ids are stable. Never renumber. A row is never deleted: it is superseded.

## How to add a row

A new decision gets a row the day it is made, in the same commit as the change where there is one.

1. Pick the subsection. Take the next free number of its prefix (for example `DAS-086`).
2. Fill all eight cells. One sentence for the decision, in the present tense, saying what the
   software does. The date the decision was made. Who decided. The basis as recorded (evidence,
   measurement, citation actually read, or convention); if there is none, write `basis not
   recorded`. Where the evidence lives. The status. A phrase for the Methods.
3. If it replaces an earlier decision, change that row's Status to `superseded by <new id>` and
   leave the rest of that row as it is.
4. If it answers an open decision, remove its line from "Open decisions" at the end.
5. No names, e-mail addresses, keys or tokens, private links, or names of unpublished data sets.
   The repository is public.

Unwanted-variation removal has its own decision record, rows M1 to M14, in section 6 of
`docs/qa/workflow-execution/kit/kit-124/design-review-20261118.md`. New decisions of that kind are
added there first and referenced from subsection 4 here.

| MIS-001 | **Proteomics DIA (IQ route), peptide imputation.** Imputation is a deterministic technical-replicate mean on the raw quantity scale: within an explicitly declared technical-replicate group of at least two distinct design runs, a missing value is replaced by the mean of the observed values of the same peptide when the group's missing fraction is `<=` the maximum (default 0.5, so exactly 50% missing is eligible); an all-missing or single-run group is never imputed; duplicate run-feature rows fail; every generated value is flagged `is_imputed = TRUE`; without declared technical replicates the step is skipped with a recorded reason. | VALR-020 | **Simulator S1 (classic proteomics), parameters.** A log2 protein matrix of 1,000 proteins: abundance mu_i ~ N(22, 2^2); residual variance scaled inverse chi-square (d0 = 4, s0 = 0.25; median 0.0745); normal residuals; 2 groups of 6; 20% true effects of \|1\| log2 on the treated group, half up; one unwanted factor with loadings N(0, tau^2), strength tau^2 / median residual variance = 3 (tau = 0.473), sample correlation with the group indicator exactly rho (centre 0); intensity-dependent missingness P(missing) = plogis((lod - value) / 1) with lod solved for the target share (centre 25%), then a protein is kept when at least half of each group's samples are observed. Oracle controls: 50 proteins without an effect, among those observed in every sample; degraded set: 40 of those plus 10 true effects. Cell C6: residual variance split 75% biological and 25% technical. Three-factor cell (stress cell S4): "each of strength 3". | 2026-11-16 | not recorded (parameter table of the script header) | The simulator's parameter table | docs/qa/workflow-execution/kit/kit-124/sim/s1_classic.R (header); docs/qa/workflow-execution/kit/kit-124/s1-pilot/; `docs/qa/workflow-execution/kit/kit-124/KIT-124-rev1.4-ticket-20261118.md` | in force. ## Appendix A. Contradictions and supersessions, by subsection

Where two sources disagree, or a later decision replaced an earlier one, both rows are kept in the tables above. This appendix lists the pairs and says which is current.

### 1. Data import and filtering

- IMP-016 superseded by IMP-017: lipid/metab zeros parked (2026-11-11), then read as missing (2026-11-15). One reader (E1a) had IMP-017 as "decided, not yet implemented"; the code site exists (`R/utils_workflow_omics_import.R:362-390`, `:528-533`), so it is in force.
- IMP-018 superseded by IMP-019: two readers converted and three silently NA'd text (2026-11-08), then every proteomics reader refuses non-numeric text (2026-11-11).
- IMP-025 extended (not replaced) by IMP-026: the count policy of 2026-10-07 gained non-finite and zero-library refusals on 2026-11-06.
- IMP-035 superseded by the proteomics design-save preflight landed in KIT-118 M4 (executive call 2, 2026-11-15). The later decision has no source read in this subsection (parked-20261113.md row 2); 
- IMP-067 (q-value step per row, 2026-10-09 audit) superseded in that part by IMP-043 (feature group, 2026-10-13). The rest of IMP-067 stands.
- IMP-051 and IMP-053: the non-exact rollup arm was first guarded (2026-10-08), then its GUI caller removed (2026-10-11); the guard is still in the code. Not a conflict.
- IMP-083 (default `whole`) superseded by IMP-084 (`partitioned` by default) for the lipid/metab intensity filter.
- IMP-085 superseded by IMP-086 (`fastduckdb` needed at any width, not only above 64 columns).
- IMP-061 then IMP-080: the `ceiling()` removal reached proteomics on 2026-10-09 and lipid/metab on 2026-10-31 (decided 2026-10-28). Sequence, not conflict.
- IMP-072: conflict inside one row on the proteomics correlation default (0.75 in the 2026-09-11 contract and the proteomics helper functions; 0.5 in the S4 generic, the lipid method, the shared normalisation panel's slider and the KIT-054 run). Not settled: which default the proteomics GUI applies was not traced.
- IMP-047: the plan's packaged cRAP list was never shipped (committed README); the plan text and the package disagree, the package is current.
- IMP-041: the historical browser helper ran rollup before protein evidence; the plan and the current tab order put evidence first.
- IMP-065: the ticket left `legacy` as the default of the sample filter; the registry default is now `physical` (switched later, source not in this subsection).

Settled items the readers had flagged:
- DIA-NN q-value thresholds: fixed at 0.01. `R/func_prot_qc_peptide_confidence_filters.R:4` holds the constant, `:6-35` stops on any other value ("DIA-NN identification q-value thresholds are fixed at 0.01 ..."), `:121-123` overwrites the arguments, the GUI passes the constant (`R/mod_prot_qc_peptide_qvalue.R:255-257`). The "0.05 shows user_set" fixture of KIT-027 cannot run through this kernel; the three keys in `config.ini` are fields only (IMP-042).
- Protein intensity filter defaults: both figures are right for different layers. GUI defaults are 2 replicates per group, 2 groups, percentile 1 (`R/mod_prot_qc_protein_intensity.R:57-68`, `:88-90`); the percentages are derived from those counts and the design (`R/func_general_parameter_helpers.R:255-278`) and overwrite the config's 60 / 60 / 1 (`inst/config/config.ini:95-99`). 33.333% is what groups of three give (my arithmetic, not in a source). The helper's own argument defaults are 1 / 50 / 1 (`R/func_prot_qc_filtering_helpers.R:164-166`) (IMP-071).
- Lipid/metab zeros read as missing: code site located, `R/utils_workflow_omics_import.R:60`, `:75` (`zero_is_missing = TRUE`), `:362-390`, `:528-533` (negative refusal); notice at `R/mod_omic_import_feature_table.R:363` (IMP-017).
- Lipid/metab intensity filters counting numeric annotation columns: still so. Four sites select `names(assay_table)[sapply(assay_table, is.numeric)]` (`R/func_lipid_s4_normalization_methods.R:931`, `R/func_metab_s4_qc_methods.R:84`, `R/func_lipid_qc.R:47`, `R/func_metab_qc_filtering_helpers.R:20`). No source read records a correction (IMP-082).
- Lipid import formats: six (MS-DIAL, Progenesis QI, XCMS, Compound Discoverer, LipidSearch, Other/Custom), `R/utils_omic_gui_config.R:1757-1759`; metab five (no LipidSearch), `:1983-1984`. The "three" of the KIT-101 scoping note is out of date (IMP-001).
- Date of the DIA-NN zero-as-missing call: the user approved it on 2026-11-12 (ticket KIT-118, section "Added 2026-11-12 ... user approved", and the code comment "user, 2026-11-12"); it was then parked for the re-record (parked-20261113.md, row 1), confirmed by the executive call of 2026-11-15 and landed that day; accepted with its missed memory gate on 2026-11-16. Both dates are correct for different events (IMP-015).
- Also found: the LFQ and TMT zero rules are at `R/func_prot_import_readers.R:392-393`, `:525-526` and `R/func_prot_import_tmt.R:176-178` (two readers had not located them); the DIA route labels are at `R/utils_omic_gui_config.R:1497-1498`, as quoted (IMP-004).

### 2. Normalisation

- NRM-008 (proteomics keeps its own normalisation frame, P-20) superseded by NRM-009 (KIT-120, shared frame; a cross-check of the sources) and, for transcriptomics, by NRM-031 (KIT-110).
- NRM-011: "RUV-III as covariates of the model, never a correction" (kit-053/outcome.md) no longer holds; KIT-056 added a correction mode. Kept inside the row; the RUV subsection owns it.
- NRM-014: the sources differ on cyclic loess on the limpa route ("close" in KIT-114; "no offered method is exact" in audit A101-04; "every non-default choice is approximate" in KIT-101). The GUI label marks only quantile and scale (code agrees with KIT-114/116: `R/mod_prot_qc_protein_normalisation.R:44-50`). Not settled by a grep.
- NRM-014: the approval of F-23 was recorded as "unverified" earlier on 2026-11-11 (user: "i think so? i cant remember."); the later "take all recommendations" answer the same day supersedes that. Row carries the later answer.
- NRM-020: AUD-40 says the partitioned variants have `whole` as the default; that default is superseded by `partitioned` (KIT-089; a cross-check of the sources). ITSD itself stays `whole`.
- NRM-034 and NRM-035: the ticket listed the PCA threshold as a repair to make; the outcome reverted it. The fixture difference first blamed on the threshold came from NRM-035 (`drop = FALSE`).
- NRM-033: config `[plotRle] yaxis_limit=-3,3` against -6 to 6 in the GUI calls (display only).
- NRM-005, NRM-024: RUV defaults restated here are re-decided by the KIT-124 gate; these rows only restate.
- NRM-025 is a validation binding, not the shipped defaults.

### 3. Missing values and imputation

- MIS-003 (manuscript stops naming a DIA imputation method, 2026-10-14) superseded by MIS-004 and MIS-007 (2026-10-19).
- MIS-010 (fastlimpadpc default, user, 2026-10-19) superseded by MIS-011 (limpa default as shipped, 2026-10-21, user away) superseded by MIS-012 (fastlimpadpc where installed, one Rayon thread, user, 2026-10-24). Code agrees with MIS-012; the comment at `inst/config/config.ini:70` is stale.
- MIS-018 (own NIPALS, "not a strict clean-room") superseded as an implementation by MIS-021 (clean-room rewrite, same results).
- MIS-021, decided by: the plan decision record says user; the KIT-090 ticket reader says "default taken by best practice and recorded". Not settled by the sources read; the row says so.
- MIS-008 against NRM-010: `log2(x + 1)` for unlogged input in the limpa method against "no offset, non-positive to NA" on the DIA_LIMPA route. Both are in the code (`R/func_pept_s4_missingness.R:193,204`; `R/utils_workflow_prot_declarations.R:494`); the route delivers an already logged matrix per KIT-047, so the `+ 1` branch should not be reached there. That last step was not traced in code.
- MIS-014: the 10,800 s worker deadline for the DPC step (set by KIT-053) was dropped by KIT-057; the setting row belongs to another subsection.
- MIS-019: 2 against 5 components (see above); kept as one row because the code holds both.
- MIS-009 against MIS-008: `dpc_slope = 0.8` is a declared parameter in KIT-047 and "the fallback when estimation fails" in the 2026-09-11 contract; the ticket does not explain the relation. Check the method before describing it.

### 4. Unwanted-variation removal

- UVR-008, UVR-023, UVR-034, UVR-041, UVR-042 (today's designs per omic): in force in the code, superseded as defaults by M2 / M4 / M5, kept as Legacy by M3.
- UVR-012 superseded by UVR-013 (complete-case controls: executive call, then measured and not adopted); UVR-013's control rule superseded as the default by M2.
- UVR-014 superseded by UVR-015 and UVR-020, then M2, M3 (withdrawn figures).
- UVR-015 (parked row 11) and UVR-020 (KIT-123 R3): findings in force; the open question superseded by M1 to M4.
- UVR-016 superseded by UVR-017 (k bound) and UVR-018 (levels restored).
- UVR-016 / UVR-017: k on the DIA full corpus is written 44 in KIT-118 and parked row 14, 45 in KIT-123 for the same journey. Not settled.
- UVR-017: the default k rule superseded by M5; UVR-018 extended by M8.
- UVR-032 superseded by UVR-033 (transcriptomics, more than two groups).

| VAL-50 | RUV options on the Quartet RNA reference materials (KIT-164): where the simulation gate G-D shows that a jackknife interval's bound misses more often than its limit under the simulated batch mechanisms (the auditor's sketch: a lower-bound miss of about 0.051 to 0.056 against 0.035 under mirrored skew), the affected steps are read with a calibrated, wider interval instead of the ticket stopping there. The multiplier c is the smallest value on a 0.01 grid at which every simulated case has a one-sided miss of at most 0.030 at every bound the step uses and two-sided coverage of at least 0.93 on simulation seeds 1 to 4,000; it is confirmed on seeds 4,001 to 8,000 (at most 0.035, at least 0.93). If the confirmation fails, c becomes the larger of its calibration value and the smallest value meeting the criterion on all 8,000 data sets, and every interval read at it is labelled "calibrated in sample" (its coverage is then not independently confirmed). c is never below the table's t quantile and never above 4.0; with no passing value the E/N batch table stops the ticket and a secondary table reads "coverage not shown". | VAL-51 | Enrichment of gene and protein sets on the factors of an integration (Gene Ontology, KEGG, Reactome): the test of record is a competitive gene-set test that estimates the correlation between the features of a set and widens the test accordingly, applied to each feature's regression on the factor (limma's `camera`, Wu and Smyth 2012, which its authors describe as suitable for any experiment that can be represented by genewise linear models; applying it to the regression on a factor follows from that statement and is not itself a result reported in the paper. Permutation of the factor's scores across samples is not offered: the factor is estimated from the same data, the permutation does not refit the model, and free permutation ignores the design's group structure. These reasons are reasoning, not evidence against it: PCGSE reports such a permutation near nominal in its own simulation (0.05 and 0.014 at a nominal 0.05; that simulation had 75 samples and 200 features, so it does not show the behaviour at the 11 to 12 samples of this programme's study). If the correlation-estimating test does not hold its error rate in its own simulation check at the study's sample sizes, the fallback is the preset-correlation form (`cameraPR`), labelled as such, under the failing-test rule of VAL-34. Whatever the test, a result on a factor learned from the same data is an exploratory ranking aid and is worded so. | VAL-73 | Lipidomics and metabolomics log2 step: plain log2(x) by default in place of log2(x + 1). Rule: at offset 0 a missing cell stays missing, a cell of 0 or below and a NaN or infinite cell become missing and are counted (warning `omics_log2_nonpositive` for direct callers; the counts in the step log in the application); any offset above 0 runs the earlier code path and returns the earlier object, so a record made with an offset replays exactly; an offset below 0 is refused (`omics_log2_offset_invalid`); an error of the transform stops (`omics_log2_failed`, the silent fallback removed). The offset leaves the normalisation tab; a project whose record used one says so. Statistical position: zeros are read as not detected at import (IMP-017) and not imputed, so a feature is tested only where it was measured (limma on available values) and a fold change can be underestimated when values fall below the detection limit in one group; features not tested for an unobserved group are counted in the DA summary; no variance-stabilising transform is offered (limma-trend with robust hyperparameters models variance against mean). Measured effect: on intensity-scale data (every value at least 1e4) at most 1.4247e-4 log2 (T6; bound 1.4427e-4); on the four GUI-entry lanes (intensities 2.4e3 and above) no call changes (their DA summaries are identical at offset 1 and at plain log2, control run 45148367369); the change at the log step is at most about 6e-4 log2 (a bound from the smallest value, not measured); on two simulated concentration-scale data sets with no true difference between the groups (one draw each; T11), through the default route (ITSD, cyclic loess, legacy RUV-III Automatic), the largest change of a log2 value is 6.5 to 6.9, and every call at q < 0.05 is a false discovery: with the offset 165 and 0 features were called, with plain log2 16 and 37 (the legacy RUV choice moved from k 7 to 2 and controls 17 % to 1 %, and from k 1 to 2 and 12 % to 1 %); the largest change of a fold change was 29.7 and 196.7 log2 units. One configuration check came out beyond its prediction (bias target -0.0112 against a predicted -0.0077 with standard deviation 0.0009 over feature draws); the likely cause is the one seeded feature draw, not confirmed; the cell's composition is shown independently by its tests and the other two targets match their predictions. The paired differences in false discovery proportion between the two control rules are expected to be zero-inflated and right-skewed (many data sets without a false call in either arm). In the auditor's simulation the studentised mean tested at the margin by sign flips then has a one-sided size of up to 0.099 (0.063 to 0.075 under exponential differences) against a nominal 0.05; the excess belongs to the test, not to the sample-size re-estimation. | VAL-217 | INT-28's limitations of the integration model, for users of the Integration tabs and readers of the integration report (KIT-239, OD-2) and for the help page `?integrationTrainModel` (KIT-234): one answer for both homes. INT-28's content was accepted on 2026-11-21; the workbook sentences that carried it stop shipping (VAL-209), and two of them state more than the evidence. Decided: (a) the six evidence-based sentences of AUDIT-KIT-239-plan-20261125 section 6 (KIT-239 section 7, rows 1 to 6) are the basis; the workbook's sentences are not used. In substance: (1) how small a pattern the model can find depends on the number of samples: in this software's simulations with 20 samples (two groups of 10), a pattern carried only by the two smallest of four data sets, in a tenth of their features, each changed by about two-thirds of its measurement noise, was recovered closely (a correlation of at least 0.9 with the true pattern) in at most 2 of 10 simulated data sets in each of the 28 settings tried, which did not include the current default feature selection; with 60 samples in 7 to 10 of 10; with the default settings a pattern as large as the noise was recovered in 26 to 29 of 30 at 20 samples; MOFA2's documentation asks for more than 15 samples; the factors are descriptive; (2) missing values are left out, which assumes they are missing at random; values too low to measure are not modelled as such, so estimates for low-abundance features can be biased; MOFA2 fills means only to compute where training starts; (3) where runs were averaged, each average uses only the runs in which the value was measured and is too high when low values are missing; (4) one group, normally distributed (Gaussian) variation, one input per omic, and the integration fills in no missing value itself; (5) the model is identical to the adapted analysis script's given its settings, checked on simulated data only, a check of the software and not of any biological result, and the default settings differ from the script's; (6) enrichment needs external services (STRING, by default version 12.5; KEGG or Reactome tables) and depends on the release used, which is recorded with each result. What must survive any shortening: the strength in words that are not 'weak', the criterion 'recovered closely', 'at most 2 of 10', 'the settings tried did not include the default selection', and the 60-sample and default-settings contrasts. (b) Added to sentence 4: 'values that an omic's own workflow estimated before saving are treated as measured' (the proteomics summary can export its imputed state and the DIA route offers replicate-mean imputation, so the missing-at-random sentence does not cover such values). (c) Added to sentence 5: 'The default settings were chosen from simulations of one design, not from real data.' (INT-23, INT-24). Final polish the owner's (VAL-41). Not measured, and not to be implied: the shipped settings on the weaker pattern; sample sizes between 20 and 60 | 2026-11-25 | owner: 'yes to all' to the coordinator's numbered list (item 8); AUDIT-KIT-239-plan-20261125 section 6; KIT-239 sections 7 and 14 (OD-2) | decided; by KIT-239 (tab and report) and KIT-234 (help page), before the release commit |

| VAL-221 | Integration: the defaults INT-14 left open (the number of seeds, the seed rule, the pairing rule) and the 'provisional' marks (KIT-238 OQ-3, with the corrections of its Re-check 1, R1-04 and R1-05, AUDIT-KIT-238-plan-20261125). Today 5 models are trained, from the declared seed 20261119 and the next four whole numbers; the reported model (weights, variance explained, file, record) is the declared seed's; of the other four only their factors and rounds are kept, and each reported factor's median and lowest agreement with them is shown. Decided: (1) the declared seed's model stays the reported one: it is fixed before training, reproducible from one stated number and does not depend on how many seeds are trained. Keeping instead the model with the highest final ELBO is MOFA2's own convention (`select_model`) and a selection on the training objective, not on results; it is not taken because in KIT-151's check the ELBO spread across seeds was 2e-7 to 1.6e-4 of the ELBO while weak factors differed (absolute correlation down to 0.002), so the ELBO barely separates the solutions, and it would make the reported model depend on the number of seeds and re-record `mofa_reference/`. Added: each seed's final ELBO is kept beside its rounds, so where the reported model's fit ranks can be shown; this changes neither the reported model nor the reference. Stated as a limitation: the stability table describes only the reported model's factors, so a factor that other seeds find but the reported model lacks is not shown (KIT-151c: a planted factor recovered in 4 of 10 seeds in one cell). (2) The number of seeds stays 5. Four comparisons show plainly the gap KIT-151 found between strong factors (absolute correlation at least 0.99 across seeds) and weak ones (down to 0.002); 10 seeds would give the median and lowest agreement over 9 other models instead of 4, at about twice the training time, and the lowest of more correlations is lower by construction, so the 'lowest agreement' column is not comparable between seed counts. (3) Pairing stays greedy and one-to-one by absolute Pearson correlation over the samples both models have, the most similar pair first. Both biases are stated: optimal assignment maximises the total agreement and can lower a strong factor's value slightly to raise a weaker one's; the greedy rule can understate a weaker factor whose best partner was taken by a stronger one; the two differ only when reported factors compete for one partner. (4) The 'workbook (provisional)' and other 'provisional' marks on the integration defaults are reworded so that they neither say 'awaiting the user' nor point to a workbook (none ships, VAL-209), the values they mark kept (KIT-238 13.1, option (a)); the wording is the owner's (VAL-41). | VAL-330 | The lipidomics and metabolomics sample-correlation filter after RUV (AUDIT-KIT-255-impl-20261126 I08; derived, not run). RUV-III absorbs a single sample's anomaly into one of its k factors: on KIT-255's fixture the anomalous sample correlated 0.991 with its replicates after RUV in the anomalous assay, against 0.985 for its genuine values in the other assay. The filter after RUV can therefore fail a sample only if k = 0 or RUV is skipped, more samples deviate than there are factors, the deviation does not show in the control features, or other residual structure is larger. Consequence by route: with RUV factors in the model the sample is in effect left out of that assay's test; on the legacy RUV-III-C route its corrected values approximate its replicates' mean and the test counts it as a replicate, so standard errors are too small by a derived factor of 0.775, 0.845 and 0.905 at 3, 4 and 6 samples per group. Decided: it is STATED now (NEWS and the user guide, as a limit of the correlation filter after RUV) and MEASURED on runners before the release (its own measurement ticket); the method order is not changed (the correlation is not moved before RUV) and no before-and-after display is added by this decision | 2026-11-26 | owner, 2026-11-26: '1.', in reply to the coordinator's four numbered options on this point (1 = state now and measure before the release) | decided; statement drafted in KIT-255's NEWS and wording; measurement ticket KIT-275 to be written |

'Safe' needs every one of about 150 safety classifications per arm to meet its edge by a one-sided 97.5 % limit at R = 400. For the any-call rule S2, an arm at exactly the nominal 0.05 per family meets it in one condition with probability 0.90 (two families) and 0.80 to 0.98 (three), but in all 30 null conditions with probability about 0.01 to 0.15; at 0.04 per family 0.87 to 0.99. S5 needs zero attributable extreme errors in 60 conditions of 400 data sets (probability 0.79 at a per-data-set rate of 1e-5, 0.09 at 1e-4); arms at R = 100 can never meet it. | KIT-147 (what an omic's integration input is on disk: contract v2) | Each omic's Summary writes `integration/<omic>/` as schema `multischolar.integration_input.v2`: `integration_input.json` (the manifest), `samples.parquet` (the design of the runs, text columns), and per data set `matrix_<view>.parquet` (wide: `feature_id` as text, then one double column per run in the samples table's order) and `features_<view>.parquet` (`feature_id`, `display_name`, annotation, text). Every Parquet file is format version 2.6, snappy-compressed, in row groups of 10,000 rows, with no R metadata, so the same table gives the same bytes on the same platform's Arrow build and the same content on every platform (a file's SHA-256 identifies it on the machine that wrote it and travels with the project; another platform's Arrow may compress the same pages into other bytes); the manifest records that layout (`parquet`), each data set's row and run counts and row-group count, and every file's SHA-256. Values are stored as written, bit for bit (missing values, NaN, -0 and values below 1e-148 included, which the v1 text tables could not keep). The reader checks the manifest, every SHA-256, the samples table, and per data set the matrix's schema (ids first, the runs once each in the samples' order, doubles), shape and row groups and its feature ids (present, non-empty, unique, the same and in the same order in the features file) without loading a matrix. A v1 folder (TSV tables) was only written by development builds and is refused in words: save that omic's Summary again | 2026-11-20 | implementation (KIT-147) under INT-10 | code on `kit-147-integration-parquet`; not merged |
| KIT-147 (the streamed import) | The integration import reads each data set from its Parquet file row group by row group (at most 10,000 features at a time) and writes it into the integration store as a table; no whole input file is read as text and no whole data set is held in R during the import (the largest object is one row group: 10,000 features by the data set's runs). The inputs state is then committed with those tables in place of the in-memory matrices; a file imported again (same SHA-256) reuses its stored table. The values the model reads from the store are those of the file, so alignment and model are unchanged | 2026-11-20 | implementation (KIT-147) under INT-10 | code on `kit-147-integration-parquet`; not merged |

A first pass over the pages averages the technical replicates, drops the features observed in fewer than two biological samples and, under per-feature scaling, those without variance, and keeps one number per remaining feature (the statistic the most-variable selection ranks by); the selection is then taken once over the whole data set from those numbers; a second pass keeps the selected features, Z-scored under per-feature scaling. Every rule is the whole-matrix alignment's, applied feature by feature through the same functions, and the result is shown `identical()` to it (not merely equal within a tolerance) on a test data set built for the purpose: 12,000 features by 70 runs (two pages, two column blocks), sixty features of one variance across the page boundary with a cap that cuts inside them, internal standards, sparse and constant features on both pages, under both scaling settings and both missing-sample rules; and the model trained through either alignment is the same model. The choice of alignment is not a parameter of the model and not part of its identity. The model still needs the selected data in memory (MOFA2 takes whole matrices): only the selected features of each data set are held, never a data set whole | 2026-11-20 | implementation (KIT-149) under the plan of 2026-11-20 (item C) | code on `kit-149-partitioned-alignment`; not merged; identity shown on a runner (run-tests 44668558288, the test failing on three deliberately broken mechanisms), and the partitioned alignment is now the default (the whole-matrix one stays selectable as the variant `whole`) |
